data.narrative:
MacroFab is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Chris Church that has raised $141M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 9 total firms—1 public and 8 private—spanning the robotics and manufacturing sector at similar stages, including peers such as Hadrian, Agile Robots, Nimble Robotics, Divergent, and Exotec.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $141M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement, implying a valuation of $240M. Peer-median analysis examines three same-sector, same-stage comparables: Hadrian ($1.6B), Agile Robots ($1.0B), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B). The median valuation across this set is $1.0B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $1.6B.

The triangulated analysis across both methods supports a valuation range of $204M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $620M. The substantial spread reflects a core tension: stage-progression anchored to historical fundraising suggests $240M, while peer multiples suggest significantly higher values in the $1.0B range. Key uncertainties include relative market position and unit economics versus the peer set, as well as revenue trajectory assumptions implicit in peer valuations. Closer examination of comparable company growth rates and capital efficiency would be necessary to narrow this range.
